children: Japanese commercial banks charged an average of 2.120% on new loans to companies in September, the highest rate in 30 years, the Bank of Japan said,

The rise follows two policy rate increases by the central bank this year, in June and September. Those moves took its benchmark rate to 1.25%, a level last seen almost 31 years ago, and banks have been passing the higher costs on to business borrowers.
The September average was 0.338 percentage point above the August figure. The rate has not been higher since May 1996, when it stood at 2.146%.

The largest lenders raised rates fastest. At city banks the average climbed 0.409 point to 2.291%. Regional banks lifted their rate by 0.322 point to 2.053%, and second-tier regional banks added 0.129 point to reach 2.028%.
The central bank's data showed that loan rates at the major banks are closely tied to market interest rates, which accounts for their quicker adjustment.
Higher borrowing costs have not slowed credit growth so far. Total bank lending has kept expanding because companies remain eager to fund capital investment.

title: Japan corporate lending rates reach 30-year high
